info.title: CF Meet Calling service API
info.description: HTTP surface exposed by services/calling (Part C sections 15-25): the health endpoint; the call API (list, get, available actions); application call creation (POST /v1/calls) and control (accept, decline, cancel, end, hold, resume, transfer, session removal, media credentials); the application endpoint registry and signaling-credential minting; the endpoint's own signaling operations (WebSocket channel, offer recovery, accept / decline, media credentials) authenticated by a short-lived signaling credential; the media connection gateway, which admits every media signaling connection against authoritative state before the media server is contacted; and the media provider callback, authenticated by the provider's signature. There is no generic state mutation: a client never sends a state, a scope, an authorization result, a route, a provider, a room, a media identity, a permission or a telephone number. Tenant, application and environment scope comes only from the authenticated credential; a call, principal, endpoint, offer or session of another scope is answered exactly like a missing one (404). Every state-changing command carries expectedVersion (the single concurrency mechanism); Idempotency-Key is required for call creation and transfer and honoured on every other command (a replay returns the recorded response with Idempotent-Replayed: true; a different request under the same key is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT). Every response carries an x-request-id header with the server-generated request id; a well-formed client x-request-id is echoed as x-client-request-id.

post.description: Receives a restrictive enforcement command from Privacy Relay (contract cfmeet.privacy-relay.enforcement-command). Requires an internal service token, the receiver-granted permission communication-authority.enforce (grantable only to cfmeet.privacy-relay) and a signed delegated platform context (the only scope). Calling finds its own protected calls by the opaque communication_context_ref / privacy_relay_ref it stored, skips calls authorized at or after the enforced version, and terminates the rest through the ordinary call commands (pre-answer CANCEL; answered / connected / held / transferring END -> ENDING -> cleanup -> ENDED). Deduplicated by enforcementEventId: a replay returns the recorded result without touching calls again. It can never grant authority.

200.description: Applied (or the recorded result of the same enforcement event).

post.description: Receives one normalized event from Telephony's outbox (contract cfmeet.telephony.event): requires an internal service token with the receiver-granted permission telephony-event.apply (grantable only to cfmeet.telephony). Calling deduplicates by eventId, applies per-leg sequences in order (an older one is STALE), quarantines events that do not match an execution it commanded (UNMATCHED) and never resurrects a terminal Call (IGNORED_TERMINAL; a late success triggers cleanup of the execution). Every delivered event is answered 200 with its disposition; only a failure to record it is an error (Telephony retries). Telephony never sets Calling state: each event is validated against Calling's own state machines. No telephone number, provider id or SIP data exists in the body.

200.description: Recorded with its disposition (APPLIED, DUPLICATE, STALE, IGNORED_TERMINAL or UNMATCHED).

post.description: Telephony offers an inbound public call to a relay number (contract cfmeet.telephony.inbound-offer). Requires an internal service token with telephony-inbound.offer (grantable only to cfmeet.telephony). Calling re-checks CURRENT Privacy Relay authority (CALLBACK_RELAY route), the routing policy (PSTN_TO_APP), the environment's configured inbound owner and the spend policy, then creates ONE canonical Call (origin PUBLIC_INBOUND; the caller is a TELEPHONE_ENDPOINT principal referencing only the opaque ContactReference) and rings the authorized application principals. Idempotent per telephonyLegId. Refusals reveal nothing to the caller.

200.description: The canonical Call and public CallLeg (the same for a repeated offer).

get.summary: List the caller's calls, or one principal's call history (newest first, keyset pagination)
get.description: Requires the calls.read scope. Ordered by createdAt descending, then callId descending. Only the bounded filters below are accepted; unknown or repeated query parameters are rejected with 400. The cursor is opaque, carries position only and never scope. Part F §62: with principalId the response is that principal's canonical call history (CallHistoryList): only Calls it participates in, each with its participant-relative direction and outcome derived from Call evidence (never from push or realtime delivery), safe enterprise labels, the voicemail link for mailbox owners and recording availability; direction / outcome / missed need principalId. enterpriseDestinationType + enterpriseDestinationId narrow either listing.

parameters.description: Page size (default 25, at most 100).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque nextCursor of the previous page.

parameters.name: createdAfter
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound of createdAt (RFC 3339).

parameters.name: createdBefore
parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound of createdAt (RFC 3339).

parameters.name: principalId
parameters.description: Part F §62: this principal's history (a principal of the credential's scope; any other id yields an empty page).

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: History only (needs a principal): INBOUND (the principal was a recipient) or OUTBOUND (the principal initiated the Call).

parameters.name: outcome
parameters.description: History only (needs a principal): the participant outcome derived from Call evidence.

parameters.name: missed
parameters.description: History only (needs a principal): true lists only Calls the principal missed (outcome MISSED); false excludes them.

parameters.description: With enterpriseDestinationId: only Calls routed through this enterprise destination (an extension — as dialed or reached —, a ring group, a queue, an IVR flow or a voicemail mailbox of the same scope). Never a public contact.

parameters.name: enterpriseDestinationId
parameters.description: With enterpriseDestinationType: the destination's id.

200.description: One page of calls (CallList), or with principalId one page of history (CallHistoryList).

post.summary: Create and ring an application call
post.description: Requires calls.write and an Idempotency-Key. Creates the Call (REQUESTED), records the APP_DIRECT_V1 authorization, resolves the target principals inside the credential's scope, selects the APPLICATION route, prepares the Call's media resource through the configured media provider, authorizes the initiator's session and rings every eligible endpoint of every target (one offer each, server-owned expiry). Answers 201 with the call (normally RINGING). A replay with the same key returns the recorded response; the call is never created twice.

201.description: The call was created (or the recorded response of an identical earlier request).

get.summary: Get one call with its participants, sessions and durations
get.description: Requires the calls.read scope. A call that does not exist, belongs to another tenant, application or environment, or whose id is malformed is answered with the same 404.

parameters.name: call_id
parameters.description: CF Meet call id.

get.summary: Actions currently available on a call
get.description: Requires calls.read. Server-derived from the Call's state, its live offers, the credential's scopes and the media provider's capabilities.

post.summary: Accept a ring offer on behalf of one endpoint
post.description: Requires calls.write. Exactly one device per participant wins (single-winner arbitration in the database); the participant's other offers become ANSWERED_ELSEWHERE and lose every media path. The first winning participant moves the Call to ANSWERED. An expired offer is 410; an offer that is no longer live (cancelled, answered elsewhere, declined) is 409.

200.description: The command's result (or the recorded response of an identical earlier command).

post.summary: Decline a ring offer on behalf of one endpoint
post.description: Requires calls.write. Declines only this endpoint's offer; other devices keep ringing. The Call ends as DECLINED only when every live offer of every pending target is declined.

200.description: The command's result (or the recorded response of an identical earlier command).

post.summary: Cancel a call before it is active
post.description: Requires calls.write. Pre-active termination (REQUESTED ... ANSWERED): cancels live offers and outstanding attempts, closes route, leg and sessions and tears down the media resource. Repeating it on a CANCELLED call is a no-op.

200.description: The command's result (or the recorded response of an identical earlier command).

post.description: Requires calls.write. Moves the Call to ENDING, removes every media connection and terminates the media resource; the Call becomes ENDED only on cleanup evidence (otherwise it stays ENDING and the reconciler retries). Usage and quality are finalized.

200.description: The command's result (or the recorded response of an identical earlier command).

post.description: Requires calls.write. Enforced at the media provider: every admitted connection loses audio and video publishing (subscription unchanged) before the Call becomes HELD. A provider that cannot update permissions is 422 CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE; an unconfirmed update is 503 MEDIA_UNAVAILABLE and the Call stays CONNECTED.

200.description: The command's result (or the recorded response of an identical earlier command).

post.description: Requires calls.write. Re-derives every connection's permissions from the currently authorized server state (never from a stored pre-hold grant) and applies them at the provider before the Call becomes CONNECTED.

200.description: The command's result (or the recorded response of an identical earlier command).

post.summary: Transfer a participant's place to another principal
post.description: Requires calls.write and an Idempotency-Key. The same Call continues (TRANSFERRING): the target's endpoints are rung with TRANSFER offers; when the target joins with a media path the transferring participant is retired and the Call returns to CONNECTED. If the target declines, does not answer or cannot join, the transfer FAILS and the Call returns to its pre-transfer state (CONNECTED or HELD) when the remaining parties still have a media path.

200.description: The command's result (or the recorded response of an identical earlier command).

post.summary: Issue a media credential for a session
post.description: Requires calls.write. Issues a short-lived join credential for one session whose media access the server authorized (the initiator's session, or a participant's single winning device) while the Call is in a media state. Capabilities derive from server state only; the body must be empty. A losing, removed or ended session, or a terminal Call, is 409.

post.summary: Remove one session from a call
post.description: Requires calls.write. Ends the session and revokes its media access for ever: its credentials stop working, the provider connection is removed (or queued for enforcement) and any re-entry is evicted. The Call's state is not changed; removing a removed session again is a no-op.

200.description: The session was removed (or the recorded response of an identical earlier command).

post.summary: Register an application endpoint of a principal
post.description: Requires calls.write. The principal is resolved inside the credential's scope (unknown, foreign or inactive: 404). Registering the same endpointKey again for the same principal refreshes the endpoint (200); a key held by another principal is 409.

get.description: Requires calls.read. Only endpoints of the credential's scope; a foreign principal has none.

delete.description: Requires calls.write. The endpoint is never rung again; its live offers are cancelled and its signaling credentials stop working. Revoking a revoked endpoint is a no-op.

post.summary: Mint a signaling credential for one endpoint
post.description: Requires calls.write. Called by the application backend, which hands the short-lived credential to the device. The device never receives the platform API credential.

201.description: The signaling credential (secret: deliver it to the device only).

get.summary: Open the endpoint's realtime signaling channel (WebSocket)
get.description: Authenticated before the upgrade with the endpoint's signaling credential. Delivery only: the server sends signaling.ready, then the endpoint's realtime signals (cfmeet.calling.realtime-signal, https://schemas.cfmeet.com/calling/realtime/v1.schema.json), answers {"type":"ping"} with signaling.pong and closes with code 4001 when the credential expires. Signals are sent only after the authoritative transaction committed; a lost signal never loses state (recover with GET /v1/calling/invitations and the call API). Commands use HTTP.

101.description: Switching Protocols: the WebSocket channel is open (subprotocol cfmeet.signaling.v1 when it was offered).

get.description: Signaling credential. The endpoint's live and recently finished offers with the authoritative Call state; only unexpired RINGING offers of answerable calls are actionable. Stale client state is never trusted.

Signaling credential. Recovery after a reconnect: the canonical call history of the credential's principal (every device of it sees the same entries), with the same derivation and filters as GET /v1/calls?principalId= — a client that missed every push and realtime signal reads the authoritative missed / answered outcome here. principalId is not accepted (an endpoint reads its own principal only).

get.summary: Open a media signaling connection (SDK legacy path)
get.description: Media connection gateway (WebSocket upgrade; the media SDK's signaling protocol is relayed opaquely). Before anything reaches the media server, the presented media credential is authenticated (edge signature, expiry, resource, identity, generation) and admitted against authoritative state: the session must exist in that Call, hold media access (AUTHORIZED, not removed or ended, participant still in the Call, Call in a media state) and the credential must carry the session's CURRENT media generation. Otherwise the upgrade is refused (401; 503 when the state cannot be read: fail closed). An admitted connection is relayed with a single-use, join-only media-server token; media rights are applied server-side after the join. Every token the media server refreshes is re-checked and re-sealed with the edge key before it reaches the client, so no client ever holds a token the media server accepts directly.

101.description: Switching Protocols: the admitted connection is relayed to the media server.

400.description: Malformed request (query, or no WebSocket upgrade).

401.description: Not admitted: missing, malformed, forged or expired credential; unknown identity; foreign resource; revoked, removed or ended session; stale generation; terminal Call. Plain-text body; uniform.

503.description: Authoritative state unreadable, or the media server unreachable: refused (fail closed).

post.description: Called by the configured media provider only; authenticated by the provider's signature over the exact body (unsigned or forged: 401). Each event is recorded once (deduplicated by the provider's event id) as operational evidence: it can confirm or deny media facts of existing sessions but never creates a participant, authorizes a call, broadens a permission or resolves a principal. An unknown media identity is quarantined and removed; a late event never resurrects a terminal call.

requestBody.description: The provider's event as it defines it (at most 64 KiB), verified before it is parsed.

200.description: The event was verified and recorded (duplicates included).

post.description: Part F: Telephony offers an internal enterprise SIP dialog (contract cfmeet.telephony.enterprise). Requires an internal service token with telephony-enterprise.offer (grantable only to cfmeet.telephony). Calling binds the opaque device reference to its ACTIVE principal in the offer's scope, resolves the extension there, applies the enterprise policy and the environment's configured owner, then creates ONE canonical Call (origin ENTERPRISE_DEVICE, route class ENTERPRISE_INTERNAL; the dialog is a PRIVATE_NETWORK leg) and routes it (ring, ring group, queue, IVR). Idempotent per telephonyLegId. An unknown / foreign device or extension is 404; enterprise calling off is 422.

200.description: The canonical Call and public CallLeg (the same for a repeated offer).

post.description: Part F: one key of an enterprise SIP leg's caller for the IVR the Call waits in (contract cfmeet.telephony.enterprise). Requires telephony-enterprise.offer. The key is used once and never stored or logged; accepted=false when the Call does not wait for a key.

200.description: The canonical Call and public CallLeg (the same for a repeated offer).

post.description: Part F: Telephony delivers a finished or failed edge media capture (contract cfmeet.telephony.capture). Requires telephony-capture.deliver (grantable only to cfmeet.telephony). Only a SIP capture Calling asked for, on that leg, is accepted (anything else is 404). The audio is integrity-checked (size, SHA-256, audio/wav, bounded length) and stored in protected object storage; the message becomes READY. 200 = stored or acknowledged (the edge may delete its spool copy); 503 ARTIFACT_STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE = retry later; 400 = refused for good.

Requires enterprise.config.write. Typed rules only. isDefault makes it the environment's baseline (the previous default is cleared, a versioned change). Enabling public forwarding or granting MANAGE_PUBLIC_FORWARDING / MANAGE_RECORDING needs that capability in the current baseline (granted by a CF Meet operator): otherwise 403 ENTERPRISE_POLICY_DENIED. Audited.

post.description: Part IV L: Telephony offers an inbound call to a Digital Communications Number (contract cfmeet.telephony.inbound-offer, DcnInboundOffer). Requires an internal service token with telephony-inbound.offer (grantable only to cfmeet.telephony). Calling verifies Numbering's INBOUND_VOICE grant against Numbering's CURRENT state (grant-verifications, audience Calling); the relayed scope, number, assignment, routing revision and target must equal the verified ones (403 CALL_NOT_AUTHORIZED otherwise — never corrected). It then routes ONLY to the verified target: a principal (PSTN_TO_APP, no Privacy Relay session) or an enterprise extension / ring group / queue (enterprise router through an extension); any other target 403 PUBLIC_ROUTE_DENIED. Numbering unreachable: 503 (fail closed). Idempotent per telephonyLegId.

200.description: The canonical Call and public CallLeg (the same for a repeated offer).

cfServiceAuth.name: X-CF-Service-Authorization
cfServiceAuth.description: Internal service token (contract cfmeet.platform.internal-http). Permissions come only from Calling's trust bundle; customer credentials are refused.

platformCredential.description: Customer platform API credential issued to an application environment's service account. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer <credential>`. The roles listed in an operation's security requirement are the platform scopes the credential must hold (e.g. calls.read). Never accepted on internal routes.

signalingCredential.description: Short-lived Call Signaling Credential of one endpoint of one principal (POST /v1/calling/signaling-credentials), sent as `Authorization: Bearer <credential>`. It authenticates only that endpoint's own signaling operations and is re-checked against the endpoint, the principal and the minting credential on every use. Platform API credentials (cfmk_...) and internal service tokens are refused on these routes. Browsers, which cannot set headers on a WebSocket, offer it on GET /v1/calling/signaling as the subprotocol pair `cfmeet.signaling.v1, bearer.<credential>`.

mediaCredential.bearerFormat: media credential (JWT sealed by Calling's media edge)
mediaCredential.description: The short-lived media credential returned by a media-credentials operation, presented by the media SDK as `Authorization: Bearer <credential>` (or the `access_token` query parameter). It is sealed with Calling's media-edge key, which the media server does not know: it is usable only through this gateway, which admits the exact session generation against authoritative state on every connection and reconnection. Platform API credentials, signaling credentials and media-server tokens are refused.

mediaProviderSignature.name: Authorization
mediaProviderSignature.description: Signature of the configured media provider over the exact callback body, verified with the provider's own mechanism (a signed token carrying the body digest). No CF Meet credential is accepted on the callback route; an unsigned or forged callback is 401.

IdempotencyKey.name: idempotency-key
IdempotencyKey.description: Client-chosen key (1-255 printable ASCII characters, no spaces), sent once. The same key with the same request returns the recorded response; with a different request it is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; concurrent duplicates take effect once.

IdempotencyKeyRequired.name: idempotency-key
IdempotencyKeyRequired.description: Required. Client-chosen key (1-255 printable ASCII characters, no spaces), sent once. The same key with the same request returns the recorded response (no second call or transfer); with a different request it is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.

XClientRequestId.description: Echo of a well-formed client-supplied x-request-id (diagnostic hint only).

IdempotentReplayed.description: Present when the response is the recorded response of an earlier identical command (same Idempotency-Key).

NotFound.description: Returned for any path the service does not expose, and for a call that does not exist in the caller's scope (indistinguishable from a call of another tenant, application or environment).

MethodNotAllowed.description: Returned when the path exists but does not accept the HTTP method.

ValidationError.description: Invalid query parameters (unknown or repeated parameter, out-of-range limit, malformed cursor, filter or timestamp). Code VALIDATION_ERROR.

AuthenticationFailed.description: Missing, malformed, unknown, revoked, expired or otherwise unusable credential; uniform for every reason. Code AUTHENTICATION_FAILED.

InsufficientScope.description: The credential lacks the operation's required scope. Code INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE.

www-authenticate.description: Bearer challenge naming the required scope.

ServiceUnavailable.description: A dependency (database) is unavailable. Code SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE.

InvalidRequest.description: Malformed or unknown body field, invalid query parameter, or a missing / malformed / repeated Idempotency-Key. Code VALIDATION_ERROR.

Forbidden.description: INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE (the credential lacks the operation's scope) or CALL_NOT_AUTHORIZED (the call policy denied the call).

www-authenticate.description: Bearer challenge naming the required scope (INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE only).

CommandConflict.description: The command cannot apply to the current state: STALE_CALL_VERSION (expectedVersion is not the current version), CALL_STATE_CONFLICT, CALL_RESOURCE_STATE_CONFLICT, IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT (same key, different request), CONFLICT (the command with this key is still in progress), INVITATION_NOT_ACTIONABLE, ANSWERED_ELSEWHERE (another device of the participant won) or TARGET_UNAVAILABLE.

InvitationExpired.description: The offer expired (server-owned expiry); it can never be accepted. Code INVITATION_EXPIRED.

Unprocessable.description: CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE (the configured media provider cannot execute or enforce the operation), PARTICIPANT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED or CALL_EVIDENCE_REQUIRED.

TooManyRequests.description: RATE_LIMITED (request-rate limit) or CONCURRENT_CALL_LIMIT_EXCEEDED (the environment's concurrent-call limit).

Unavailable.description: SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE (database) or MEDIA_UNAVAILABLE (the media provider did not confirm the operation; the state is unchanged or queued for enforcement and reconciliation).

SignalingAuthenticationFailed.description: Missing, malformed, expired or no longer valid signaling credential (revoked endpoint, inactive principal, revoked minting credential), or a platform API credential. Uniform for every reason. Code AUTHENTICATION_FAILED.

EnterpriseForbidden.description: INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE (the credential lacks the operation's enterprise scope; calls.* never implies it) or ENTERPRISE_POLICY_DENIED (the organization's enterprise policy does not grant this capability or action).

EnterpriseConflict.description: VERSION_CONFLICT (expectedVersion is not the current version; nothing changed) or CONFLICT (an active name / extension number already exists, the resource is disabled, or it is still referenced).

ErrorCode.description: Stable public error codes of the Calling service.

ErrorEnvelope.description: Error response body. Messages are fixed, safe strings; authentication failures are uniform.

CallParticipant.description: A logical participant. displayName is presentation metadata only and never identifies anyone. connectedDurationMs is the union of the participant's session connection intervals (concurrent devices are not double counted).

CallSession.description: Summary of one device / network participation of a participant (its media / signaling identity is not exposed). connectionCount is the number of connection intervals opened (1 + reconnects). endpointId is the application endpoint the session runs on; mediaAccess is NONE until the server authorizes the session's media (initiator, or the participant's single winning device), REVOKED for ever after removal; mediaAdmittedAt is when the provider confirmed an admitted connection; removedAt is set when the session was removed.

Call.description: One call with participants, session summaries and durations. Durations of open connections are measured up to durationsAsOf (the call's end for terminal calls). connectedDurationMs runs from the first CONNECTED to the end (null if never connected). invitations are the Call's ring offers (one per target endpoint and ring round); transfers its application transfers.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor of the next page; null on the last page.

HistoryDirection.description: Direction of a Call relative to the principal whose history it is.

ParticipantOutcome.description: The outcome of a Call for ONE logical participant, derived from Call evidence only (participant, ring offers on every device, session connection intervals, the Call's state) — never from a push, a realtime signal or a client acknowledgement, and never stored as a flag. OUTBOUND: ANSWERED, NOT_ANSWERED (ended unanswered), IN_PROGRESS. INBOUND, first match wins: ANSWERED (an offer accepted on any of the participant's devices, or a session connected), DECLINED, ANSWERED_ELSEWHERE (the offers were won by another participant of the same answer group — a ring-group or queue colleague), RINGING (an offer is live), MISSED (offered on at least one device and every offer ended unanswered), NOT_REACHED (never offered, Call over), IN_PROGRESS. A losing device of a participant that answered is never a second (missed) entry.

HistoryDestinationType.description: Enterprise destinations a listing may be narrowed to.

CallParticipation.description: The principal's own part in the Call (one per logical participant, whatever its devices).

answeredAt.description: When the participant (any device) answered; for the initiator, when the Call was answered.

CallCounterpart.description: Another participant of the Call (internal display identity only).

CallHistoryEnterprise.description: Safe enterprise labels of an enterprise Call: the dialed internal extension (a short code or alias, never a telephone number), its label, the routing phase / outcome and the current ring group / queue labels.

CallHistoryVoicemail.description: The voicemail message left on the Call — present only for an owner of its mailbox. Its audio is reached through the authorized, audited voicemail routes (never a URL here).

CallHistoryEntry.description: A Call as it appears in one principal's history.

durationMs.description: From CONNECTED to the end of the Call; null while it lasts or if it never connected.

recordingAvailable.description: A READY call recording exists (metadata and audio through the authorized, audited recording routes).

CallHistoryList.description: One page of a principal's call history, newest Call first (createdAt DESC, callId DESC).

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor of the next page; null on the last page.
